areas.access: About 7 minutes from Shinjuku on the Odakyu Line, or 3 minutes from Shibuya on the Keio Inokashira Line.
areas.name: Shimokitazawa

shops.jp: スティックアウト
shops.note: Every item in the store is one flat price — ¥900 plus tax. Two floors of tees, denim and casual wear; the cheapest way to fill a suitcase in Shimokitazawa.
shops.txt: Mon–Fri 12:00 PM – 8:00 PM · Sat & Sun from 11:00 AM

shops.jp: ニューヨークジョーエクスチェンジ
shops.note: A legend inside a converted public bathhouse — look for the old tiled walls. Everything is priced under ¥10,000, most pieces ¥2,000–3,000, and stock turns over daily. Half price on the first Sunday of the month.

shops.jp: セカンドストリート下北沢店
shops.note: The big national resale chain, Shimokitazawa style: designer and brand pieces on one floor, street and casual on the other. Tax-free, and one of the easiest first stops for thrift beginners.

shops.jp: 原宿シカゴ下北沢店
shops.note: The biggest branch of the Harajuku Chicago family — a huge floor of American casual and workwear, plus one of Tokyo's best kimono and yukata corners for souvenirs.

shops.jp: トレファクスタイル下北沢東口店
shops.note: Treasure Factory's fashion arm, 2 minutes from the East Exit: vintage Levi's and military next to Hermès and Margiela. Tax-free, with a second Shimokitazawa branch 3 minutes south.

shops.jp: キンジ下北沢店
shops.note: Around 15,000 items on one floor, restocked daily and priced gently. Famous for its wall of patterned shirts — the easiest place in the area to dig for hours.

shops.jp: フラミンゴ下北沢店
shops.note: Hand-picked American vintage from the 1940s–80s, bought in the US and beautifully kept. The pink neon sign is a Shimokitazawa landmark; sister stores nearby cover other eras.
shops.txt: Mon–Fri 12:00 PM – 9:00 PM · Sat & Sun from 11:00 AM

shops.jp: デザートスノー下北沢1号店
shops.note: The original Desert Snow: US workwear and Americana — Carhartt, Dickies, military and denim — packed onto the 2nd floor. Several sister branches dot the neighborhood.

areas.walk: Tokyo's thrift capital. Shops ring the station in every direction — the big chains on the south and east streets, indie vintage on the north side (Ichibangai). Everything is within a 10-minute stroll, and most shops open around 11 AM to noon, so arrive at lunchtime and just wander.

areas.access: About 6 minutes from Shinjuku on the JR Chuo Line. Rapid trains stop at Koenji on weekends; local Sobu Line trains stop all day.
areas.name: Koenji

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-5-5
shops.jp: トレファクスタイル高円寺2号店
shops.note: The most-reviewed thrift shop in Koenji: a big, bright brand-resale floor on the PAL arcade, strong on designer labels, bags and watches. Tax-free.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-4-15
shops.jp: トレファクスタイル高円寺ヴィンテージ店
shops.note: TreFacStyle's vintage-only Koenji store: older denim, military and one-off pieces rather than current-season brands.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-27-7
shops.jp: トリップヴィンテージメンズ
shops.note: A tiny, obsessively curated men's shop: vintage brand clothing, Hermès and Tiffany jewelry, and bags. The 5.0-star rating is earned — stock is small but serious.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南3-37-1
shops.jp: トリップヴィンテージ高円寺
shops.note: The original Trip on Look Shotengai: ladies' vintage with a deep shelf of brand bags and accessories, all carefully graded.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-26-1
shops.jp: トレファクスタイル高円寺店
shops.note: The first TreFacStyle in Koenji, 2 minutes from the south exit and open from 10 AM — the earliest start on this street. Everyday brands at recycle-shop prices.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南3-57-4
shops.closed: Closed the 2nd Thursday of the month
shops.jp: サファリ高円寺1号店
shops.note: Koenji's icon. Serious American vintage — Levi's, Champion, military — bought piece by piece in the US. Six SAFARI shops in Koenji each split by genre; this is the flagship.

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-25-3
shops.jp: ビッグタイム高円寺店
shops.note: Three floors of American vintage from the team behind Grapefruit Moon — denim, sweatshirts and workwear in a big, easy-to-browse space on the main street.
shops.txt: Mon–Thu 11:00 AM – 8:00 PM · Fri–Sun until 9:00 PM

shops.addr: 東京都杉並区高円寺南4-6-1
shops.jp: スラット本店
shops.note: A Koenji institution on the PAL arcade: honest regular clothes mixed with vintage at local prices — where the neighborhood actually shops. Sister stores sit nearby.
shops.txt: From 12:30 PM · Mon–Fri until 7:30 PM, Sat until 8:00 PM

areas.walk: From the south exit, the covered PAL arcade runs straight ahead and turns into the open-air Look Shotengai — nearly every shop on this list lines that one street or sits just off it. Serious American vintage at SAFARI, brand resale at the three TreFacStyle stores, tiny specialists in between.

areas.access: Harajuku Station (Takeshita Exit) or Meiji-jingumae Station — the shops split between Cat Street, Takeshita-dori and the Omotesando side streets.
areas.lines: JR Yamanote Line · Meiji-jingumae (Chiyoda / Fukutoshin Lines)
areas.name: Harajuku & Shibuya

shops.jp: ベルベルジン
shops.note: Tokyo's most famous vintage denim shop, going since 1998. Museum-grade Levi's and American classics — prices match the quality, but even window-shopping here is an education.

shops.jp: 古着屋JAM原宿店
shops.note: A basement the size of a warehouse: row after row of imported vintage, sorted by genre, with prices below the Harajuku average. Easy to lose an hour here.

shops.jp: 原宿シカゴ原宿店
shops.note: The classic Harajuku thrift stop on Meiji-dori: American casual at fair prices, and a famous kimono corner — vintage kimono and yukata make great souvenirs.

shops.jp: キンジ原宿店
shops.note: 30,000+ items in a basement by Laforet Harajuku: used and vintage mixed, priced for digging. One of the biggest single floors in Harajuku.

shops.jp: カインドオル原宿店
shops.note: Designer brand resale on Omotesando — Comme des Garçons, Margiela, Supreme and watches, authenticated and neatly graded. Above the Lawson, on the 3rd floor.

areas.walk: The priciest vintage in Tokyo: museum-grade American denim at BerBerJin, huge imported floors at JAM and Chicago, designer resale at Kindal and KINJI. All five shops sit within a 10-minute walk of each other.

areas.access: The tour's home ground. Electric Town is anime and electronics first — clothing thrift is the exception here, not the rule.
areas.lines: JR Yamanote / Keihin-Tohoku / Sobu Lines · Tsukuba Express · Hibiya Line
areas.name: Akihabara

shops.jp: 古着屋PENNY TOKYO
shops.note: A small local shop loved for prices below the usual market rate. Akihabara's one true clothing-thrift stop — pair it with Ueno, one stop north.

areas.walk: Akihabara is light on clothes, but PENNY TOKYO is a local favorite a short walk east of the station. For a bigger hunt, Ueno & Ameyoko (next section) is one stop north.

areas.access: One of Tokyo's biggest stations. West exit (north) for BAZZSTORE; the east side for P'PARCO and Sunshine City.
areas.lines: JR Yamanote / Saikyo / Shonan-Shinjuku · Seibu · Tobu · Marunouchi / Yurakucho / Fukutoshin Lines
areas.name: Ikebukuro

shops.jp: バズストア池袋西口店
shops.note: 6,000+ items over two floors, 1 minute from the west exit — and open until 10 PM, the latest on this map. Brands and no-brand bargains side by side.

shops.jp: セカンドストリート池袋P'PARCO店
shops.note: The chain's Ikebukuro outpost in the P'PARCO basement by the east exit — a quick, reliable brand-resale stop between trains.

shops.jp: グレープフルーツムーン池袋サンシャインシティアルタ店
shops.note: 1960s–80s American and European vintage inside Sunshine City ALTA, famous for its hat wall. The most 'vintage' room in Ikebukuro.

areas.walk: A compact cluster: brand resale by the west exit, a chain outpost in P'PARCO by the east exit, and true vintage inside Sunshine City's ALTA mall.

areas.access: The Ameyoko market street runs between Ueno and Okachimachi stations — one stop north of Akihabara.
areas.name: Ueno & Ameyoko

shops.jp: 中田商店 アメ横店
shops.note: A legend since 1956, and the most-reviewed shop on this whole map: real military surplus and leather jackets from armies around the world, on the Ameyoko main street.
shops.txt: Mon–Fri 11:00 AM – 7:30 PM · Sat & Sun from 10:00 AM

shops.jp: モードオフ上野御徒町店
shops.note: Hard Off's fashion sister brand: a big bargain floor where brand pieces hide among the cheap racks. The digger's stop in Ameyoko.
shops.txt: 11:00 AM – 9:00 PM · Sat & Sun from 10:00 AM

shops.jp: マガジン上野広小路店
shops.note: One of Ameyoko's largest clothing floors — street brands, denim and vintage across a sprawling shop by the Ueno-Hirokoji crossing.

shops.jp: たんぽぽハウス上野広小路店
shops.note: 20,000+ items starting from ¥105. Not curated — a pure treasure hunt, and a Tokyo institution for it.

areas.walk: The market street under the tracks is the walk itself: military surplus at Nakata Shoten, big recycle floors at Mode Off and MAGAZINES, bargain racks at Tanpopo House. Loud, dense and fun.

checked: Shop details checked on official sites and Google listings on Nov 24, 2026.
title: Thrift Map
